events.text: We want to plan a two-week family trip to Japan
Finding the first contact a pro would call…

Hi, I'm Yuki, a Japan travel specialist. A two-week family trip to Japan can go so many directions, from neon cities to quiet countryside temples. To shape the right route, what pulls your family most?
Cities, food, and culture, Nature and hot springs
We want to plan a two-week family trip to Japan (cities, food, and culture, nature and hot springs)
Got it. For that I'm bringing in 6 Pros. I shape the route first, then rail and family needs, then your focus specialist, and finally budget and booking windows seal it.
Hi, I'm Hiroshi, your itinerary & logistics planner. Owns routing, pacing, and daily flow across regions.
Hi, I'm Kenji, your jr rail & transit expert. Owns rail passes, shinkansen routing, and regional transit.
Hi, I'm Mika, your family travel coordinator. Owns kid-friendly pacing, lodging type, and family needs.
Hi, I'm Aya, your food & dining guide. Owns reservations, dietary needs, and regional food plans.
Hi, I'm Sana, your cultural experiences curator. Owns tea, crafts, festivals, temples, and local experiences.
Hi, I'm Ren, your budget & booking strategist. Owns total budget, flight timing, and booking windows.
What daily pace fits your family best?
Balanced with breaks
Prefer two home bases or move cities often?
Three to four stops
Hiroshi has you at three to four stops. How do you want to handle luggage between stops?
Forward ahead (takkyubin)
What ages are the kids traveling?
Which lodging types interest you?
Western hotels, Ryokan with onsen
Mika noted 11 to 15 in the group. Any dietary needs or restrictions?
Picky eaters
How hands-on do you want cultural activities?
Try a few workshops
Rough total budget range for the family trip?
$15k to $25k
Noting you want balanced with breaks. When are you hoping to travel?
Spring (cherry blossoms)
That's everything we need up front. Give us a moment while your Staff writes up your plan.
Your Staff is writing your plan…
Your plan is ready.

itin: With kids 11-15 and three to four stops, plan 3-4 nights per base to avoid burnout.
Suggested flow: Tokyo 4N, Hakone 1-2N, Kyoto 4N, Hiroshima or Kanazawa 2-3N.
Build one full rest or pool day mid-trip; shinkansen transfers eat 3-5 hours door to door.
jr: For 3-4 stops in two weeks, a 14-day JR Pass at around 80000 yen rarely beats point-to-point tickets now.
Set up Suica or Pasmo on phones before arrival for subways and convenience stores.
Takkyubin runs about 2000-3000 yen per bag and takes one night; pack an overnight bag for the gap.
fam: Kids 11-15 handle ryokan etiquette well; book one or two nights, not the whole trip.
Choose a ryokan with private onsen or family bath if anyone has tattoos or shyness concerns.
Western hotels in Tokyo and Kyoto give beds, laundry, and space; book twin rooms or connecting.
food: For picky eaters, lean on tonkatsu, ramen, yakitori, curry, conveyor sushi, and depachika food halls.
Skip kaiseki as a main meal; one ryokan dinner is plenty for the experience.
Book any marquee restaurants six to eight weeks out; most izakaya and chains walk in fine.
culture: Spring workshop picks for teens: taiko drumming, soba making, samurai or ninja experience, Kyoto tea ceremony.
Cherry blossom peak shifts year to year, usually late March to early April in Tokyo and Kyoto.
Book workshops directly through shop sites or Klook rather than hotel concierges to avoid markups.
budget: $15-25k for a family of four in cherry blossom season is realistic but tight if flights are premium.
Lock flights and ryokan by December 2025 for spring 2026; prices climb sharply after January.
Expect roughly 40 percent lodging, 25 percent flights, 20 percent food, 15 percent transit and activities.

steps: Ren confirms family size, departure city, and locks the spring travel window within two weeks.
Hiroshi drafts a 14-day route with Tokyo, Hakone, Kyoto, and one western stop for review.
Kenji prices JR Pass versus point-to-point once the route is set and arranges takkyubin handoffs.
Mika books Western hotels in Tokyo and Kyoto plus one or two ryokan nights with family bath access.
Aya reserves two or three standout meals six to eight weeks out and lists picky-eater friendly spots per city.
Sana books two or three teen-friendly workshops and checks cherry blossom forecast updates in February.

note: Recorded from a real SpinUp run. The person answering was role-played by Claude.
